ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the image is a low-resolution black-and-white photograph, in which a lighter-colored fossil imprint resembling the shape of a shell or marine organism can be seen in the center of the rock surface, and the imprint is embedded in the rock matrix; the surrounding rock surface is darker in color and rough on the surface, showing a state of being exposed after denudation. Then read the question stem: this photograph was taken at Yehliu Coast Geopark, Taiwan Province, and the question stem clearly calls it a marine organism fossil, requiring judgment of the geological processes that the formation process of this landscape experienced in sequence. Reasoning: for the remains of marine organisms to form fossils, they first need to be buried by mud and sand on the seabed and form sedimentary rock, so they first experienced sedimentation; the fossil rock layer is now exposed on the coastal ground surface, indicating that the sedimentary rock layer originally located on the seabed or in a lower position later underwent crustal uplift; finally, the rock surface in the image is rough and it is located in a coastal geopark, and the fossil landscape has been exposed by stripping, indicating that it was affected by seawater erosion. Therefore, the sequence of the formation process is: sedimentation - crustal uplift - seawater erosion.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：画面中可见岩石表面中央有类似海洋生物外形的化石印痕，化石嵌在岩层/岩石基质中，周围表面粗糙，像海岸岩石被侵蚀后暴露出来。再读题干：地点是台湾省野柳海岸地质公园，照片对象明确为“海洋生物化石”，问题要求按时间顺序写出形成该景观经历的地质作用。推理路线：海洋生物遗体要成为化石，首先需在海底被泥沙埋藏并固结成沉积岩，即沉积作用；化石岩层现在出露在海岸地表，说明原本海底沉积层后来发生地壳抬升；最后图中化石景观被看见、岩面粗糙且位于海岸地质公园，说明受到海水侵蚀剥露和塑造。因此得到顺序为沉积作用—地壳抬升—海水侵蚀。

Then read the question stem: this photograph was taken at Yehliu Coast Geopark, Taiwan Province, and the question stem clearly calls it a marine organism fossil, requiring judgment of the geological processes that the formation process of this landscape experienced in sequence. Reasoning: for the remains of marine organisms to form fossils, they first need to be buried by mud and sand on the seabed and form sedimentary rock, so they first experienced sedimentation; the fossil rock layer is now exposed on the coastal ground surface, indicating that the sedimentary rock layer originally located on the seabed or in a lower position later underwent crustal uplift; finally, the rock surface in the image is rough and it is located in a coastal geopark, and the fossil landscape has been exposed by stripping, indicating that it was affected by seawater erosion. Therefore, the sequence of the formation process is: sedimentation - crustal uplift - seawater erosion.
